_api/CalloraVoipSdk.BridgeAudioFormat.ht.title: Enum BridgeAudioFormat | CalloraVoipSdk
_api/CalloraVoipSdk.BridgeAudioFormat.ht.summary: Enum BridgeAudioFormat Namespace CalloraVoipSdk Assembly CalloraVoipSdk.Client.dll Audio format delivered to and expected from a media consumer (the "bridge"/tap), such as an AI realtime bridge. When it differs from the negotiated wire codec, the SDK transcodes audio transparently so the consumer sees a single, fixed codec regardless of what the SIP peer negotiated. public enum BridgeAudioFormat Fields Passthrough = 0 Deliver and send the raw negotiated wire payload unchanged (default). The consumer must handle whatever codec was negotiated. Pcmu = 1 Always deliver and accept G.711 µ-law (PCMU, 8 kHz). Inbound wire audio is transcoded to µ-law and outbound µ-law is transcoded to the wire codec. Supported wire codecs: Opus and G.711 (µ-law/A-law); other codecs are delivered as passthrough with a warning.

Attach it to a call to start receiving. public IVideoReceiver CreateVideoReceiver() Returns IVideoReceiver CreateVideoSender() Creates a detached video sender for a call's outbound encoded video frames (transport-only; encode with your own codec). Transient: the path may recover (or be revived by an ICE restart), so the socket stays open. Distinct from Failed, which is an establishment failure before any pair was selected. _api/CalloraVoipSdk.Core.Domain.Calls.Ca.summary: Enum CallState Namespace CalloraVoipSdk.Core.Domain.Calls Assembly CalloraVoipSdk.Core.dll Lifecycle state of a call. public enum CallState Fields Connected = 3 The call is answered and media is (or is about to be) flowing. Dialing = 1 Outbound call: the INVITE has been sent and the SDK is awaiting a response. Idle = 0 No call activity; the initial state before dialing or ringing. OnHold = 4 The call is on hold; media is suspended in at least one direction. Ringing = 2 The call is ringing — outbound (remote alerting) or inbound (awaiting local accept/reject). Terminated = 6 The call has ended (hung up, rejected, or failed); a terminal state. Transferring = 5 A transfer (blind or attended) is in progress for this call.

_api/CalloraVoipSdk.Core.Domain.Calls.IC.title: Interface ICall | CalloraVoipSdk
_api/CalloraVoipSdk.Core.Domain.Calls.IC.summary: Interface ICall Namespace CalloraVoipSdk.Core.Domain.Calls Assembly CalloraVoipSdk.Core.dll A single call and its lifecycle. public interface ICall Remarks Event threading contract. Event handlers run synchronously on the SDK thread that raised the event — this is usually not the thread that created the call. Handlers therefore must not block or perform long-running/synchronous I/O: a blocked handler stalls the SDK path that raised it (SIP signaling or media), delaying every other call on the same line. Off-load real work to your own task or queue, e.g. call.StateChanged += (_, e) => _ = Task.Run(() => Handle(e));. Handlers should also not throw. See each event for the specific thread and whether it is serialized. TransferRequested is the exception to off-loading: it needs a synchronous accept/reject decision, so make that decision quickly inline (do not await long work). Error contract. The action methods split into two error styles by return type. The core lifecycle operations return Task (or Task<TResult> of bool for AttendedTransferAsync(ICall, CancellationToken)) and throw: invalid usage surfaces as InvalidOperationException (wrong state or direction), ArgumentException (invalid argument), and cancellation surfaces as OperationCanceledException; transport, timeout and unexpected transport-layer failures propagate as-is. The extended in-dialog / inbound-response operations return CallActionResult instead and do not throw for foreseeable outcomes: an invalid state or direction, a protocol rejection (for example a SIP 4xx from the peer), an invalid request, cancellation, and transport failures are all reported as a non-success CallActionResult whose Status classifies the cause (see CallActionStatus). These result-returning methods are the ones that involve a SIP round-trip whose negative answer is a normal protocol result rather than a programming error. Per-method tags below state the exact exceptions and result semantics. Properties CallId Stable identifier of this call within the SDK. CallId CallId { get; } Property Value CallId CalledNumber The dialed number (DID) an inbound call was addressed to — the user part of LocalParty (the To/Request URI). This is the number that selected the receiving line for a SIP trunk. null for outbound calls or when the URI has no user part. Defaults to null. string? CalledNumber { get; } Property Value string Direction Whether the call was placed locally (Outbound) or received (Inbound). Informational routing history, surfaced as-received. string? Default implementation returns null. string? EarlyMediaSdp { get; } Property Value string IceConnectionState Running ICE transport state for this leg (RFC 8445 / RFC 7675). Unlike the one-shot IceSnapshot (final establishment state), this tracks post-establishment changes — notably Connected → Disconnected when consent is lost. Disabled for non-ICE legs. Changes are signalled by IceConnectionStateChanged. Reports the final ICE state and the selected local/remote candidate pair. CallIceSnapshot? Must be a call created by this SDK. ct CancellationToken Cancels the transfer; on cancellation OperationCanceledException is thrown. Exceptions ArgumentException consultationCall is not a call created by this SDK. OperationCanceledException ct was canceled. BlindTransferAsync(string, CancellationToken) Performs a blind transfer to targetUri. On a successful transfer the call moves to Terminated; if the transfer fails it returns to Connected. Either way the task completes without a return value. Task BlindTransferAsync(string targetUri, CancellationToken ct = default) Parameters targetUri string The transfer target URI. ct CancellationToken Cancels the transfer; on cancellation OperationCanceledException is thrown. Returns Task Exceptions InvalidOperationException The call state is not Connected. OperationCanceledException ct was canceled. Returns Task Exceptions InvalidOperationException The call state is not Connected. MuteAsync(bool, CancellationToken) Mutes or unmutes this call's outgoing audio locally: the SDK stops (or resumes) sending this call's captured audio to the peer. Unlike HoldAsync(CancellationToken) it is not signalled to the peer (no re-INVITE), and unlike the client-wide device mute (IVoipClient.SetAudioInputMuted) it affects only this call, so on a client with several concurrent calls each mutes independently. While muted the peer receives no audio for this call (no packets are sent for the outgoing direction); inbound audio is unaffected. Local-only, so it is valid in any live state and does not throw for state; a no-op if already in the requested state. Read the current state via IsMuted. The default implementation is a no-op. Task MuteAsync(bool muted, CancellationToken ct = default) Parameters muted bool true to mute outgoing audio; false to resume. ct CancellationToken Cancels the operation; on cancellation OperationCanceledException is thrown. Returns Task RedirectAsync(IReadOnlyList<string>, int, CancellationToken) Redirects an inbound ringing call with a 3xx SIP response and contact targets. Does not throw for foreseeable outcomes; the result carries the classification instead. Task<CallActionResult> RedirectAsync(IReadOnlyList<string> contactUris, int statusCode = 302, CancellationToken ct = default) Parameters contactUris IReadOnlyList<string> The redirect contact target URIs. statusCode int The 3xx SIP status code to respond with (default 302 Moved Temporarily). ct CancellationToken Cancels the operation; reported as Canceled, not thrown. Returns Task<CallActionResult> Succeeded once the redirect is sent and the call is terminated; InvalidState when the call is not Inbound or its state is not Ringing (checked before any SIP round-trip); Canceled on cancellation; or Failed on a transport-layer failure. RejectAsync(int, string?, CancellationToken) Rejects an inbound ringing call with a 4xx/5xx/6xx SIP status. Does not throw for foreseeable outcomes; the result carries the classification instead (see the interface error contract). Task<CallActionResult> RejectAsync(int statusCode = 486, string? reasonPhrase = null, CancellationToken ct = default) Parameters statusCode int The SIP status code to reject with (default 486 Busy Here). reasonPhrase string Optional SIP reason phrase; a default is derived when omitted. ct CancellationToken Cancels the operation; reported as Canceled, not thrown. Returns Task<CallActionResult> Succeeded once the reject is sent and the call is terminated; InvalidState when the call is not Inbound or its state is not Ringing (checked before any SIP round-trip); Canceled on cancellation; or Failed on a transport-layer failure. RestartIceAsync(CancellationToken) Initiates a local ICE restart (RFC 8445 §9) on a connected, ICE-negotiated call: the SDK re-gathers on the existing media socket with fresh ICE credentials — a new ice-ufrag and ice-pwd — and re-offers them in a direction-preserving re-INVITE. The ICE role is preserved and media keeps flowing on the previously validated candidate pair until the new connectivity checks nominate a pair. Use this to recover a media path after a network change or a consent loss surfaced by IceConnectionStateChanged. Task RestartIceAsync(CancellationToken ct = default) Parameters ct CancellationToken Accepted for signature symmetry but currently not forwarded to the transport, so the restart is not cancelled via this token. Returns Task Exceptions InvalidOperationException The call state is not Connected, or ICE was not negotiated on this call. Returns Task Exceptions InvalidOperationException The call state is not Connected. SendInfoAsync(string, string, CancellationToken) Sends in-dialog SIP INFO. Does not throw for foreseeable outcomes; the result carries the classification instead. Task<CallActionResult> SendInfoAsync(string contentType, string body, CancellationToken ct = default) Parameters contentType string The INFO body content type. body string The INFO message body. ct CancellationToken Cancels the operation; reported as Canceled, not thrown. Returns Task<CallActionResult> Succeeded once the INFO is sent; Canceled on cancellation; InvalidRequest for an invalid argument; InvalidState when the transport reports the operation invalid for the current state; or Failed on a transport-layer failure. SendNotifyAsync(string, string, string?, string?, CancellationToken) Sends in-dialog SIP NOTIFY. Does not throw for foreseeable outcomes; the result carries the classification instead. Task<CallActionResult> SendNotifyAsync(string eventType, string subscriptionState, string? contentType = null, string? body = null, CancellationToken ct = default) Parameters eventType string The SIP event package the notification belongs to. subscriptionState string The Subscription-State header value. contentType string Optional body content type. body string Optional request body. ct CancellationToken Cancels the operation; reported as Canceled, not thrown. Returns Task<CallActionResult> Succeeded when the peer accepts; Rejected when the peer declines the NOTIFY; Canceled on cancellation; or Failed on a transport-layer failure. SendOptionsAsync(CancellationToken) Sends in-dialog SIP OPTIONS. Does not throw for foreseeable outcomes; the result carries the classification instead. Task<CallActionResult> SendOptionsAsync(CancellationToken ct = default) Parameters ct CancellationToken Cancels the operation; reported as Canceled, not thrown. Returns Task<CallActionResult> Succeeded when the peer accepts; Rejected when the peer declines the OPTIONS; Canceled on cancellation; or Failed on a transport-layer failure. SendSubscribeAsync(string, int, string?, string?, CancellationToken) Sends in-dialog SIP SUBSCRIBE. Does not throw for foreseeable outcomes; the result carries the classification instead. Task<CallActionResult> SendSubscribeAsync(string eventType, int expiresSeconds = 300, string? acceptHeader = null, string? body = null, CancellationToken ct = default) Parameters eventType string The SIP event package to subscribe to. expiresSeconds int Requested subscription duration in seconds (default 300). acceptHeader string Optional Accept header value. body string Optional request body. ct CancellationToken Cancels the operation; reported as Canceled, not thrown. Returns Task<CallActionResult> Succeeded when the peer accepts; Rejected when the peer declines the SUBSCRIBE; Canceled on cancellation; or Failed on a transport-layer failure. UnholdAsync(CancellationToken) Takes the call off hold and emits a local HoldStateChanged event. Task UnholdAsync(CancellationToken ct = default) Parameters ct CancellationToken Accepted for signature symmetry but currently not forwarded to the transport, so the unhold is not cancelled via this token. Returns Task Exceptions InvalidOperationException The call state is not OnHold. Events DtmfReceived Raised when a DTMF tone is received. This event may fire from two threads: the SIP signaling thread (SIP INFO tones) and the media receive thread (RFC 4733 in-band RTP events). It is therefore not guaranteed single-threaded — keep the handler thread-safe and fast. event EventHandler<DtmfReceivedEventArgs>? DtmfReceived Event Type EventHandler<DtmfReceivedEventArgs> HoldStateChanged Raised when the remote party puts the call on or off hold, and only when the hold state actually changes (a duplicate or pre-Connected hold indication does not re-raise it). Serialized on the SIP signaling thread. Like StateChanged, changes are not buffered for handlers attached later. event EventHandler<HoldStateChangedEventArgs>? HoldStateChanged Event Type EventHandler<HoldStateChangedEventArgs> IceConnectionStateChanged Raised when the running ICE transport state changes after establishment (for example Connected → Disconnected on consent loss). Fires on a media/RTCP thread, not the signaling thread. Lets the application react to a lost media path — tear down, alert the user, or (later) trigger an ICE restart. Not buffered. event EventHandler<CallIceConnectionStateChangedEventArgs>? IceConnectionStateChanged Event Type EventHandler<CallIceConnectionStateChangedEventArgs> MediaFlowChanged Raised when inbound media goes silent on a connected call, and again when it resumes (#261, ADR-069). Fires on a media/RTCP thread, not the signaling thread. Not buffered. event EventHandler<CallMediaFlowChangedEventArgs>? MediaFlowChanged Event Type EventHandler<CallMediaFlowChangedEventArgs> Remarks This is a notification, not a teardown: it fires while the peer is still demonstrably alive (RTCP keeps arriving), which is the normal state during silence suppression (RFC 3389), hold, and the bridge switch of a transfer. The application decides what silence means for its use case — play a prompt, escalate, end the call — long before the SDK's own liveness timeout would. A peer that stops sending everything is a separate matter and ends the call with a CallTerminationReason that says so. _api/CalloraVoipSdk.Core.Domain.Calls.IR.title: Interface IReferSubscription | CalloraVoipSdk
_api/CalloraVoipSdk.Core.Domain.Calls.IR.summary: Interface IReferSubscription Namespace CalloraVoipSdk.Core.Domain.Calls Assembly CalloraVoipSdk.Core.dll Live handle to the implicit subscription created by an accepted inbound SIP REFER (RFC 3515 / RFC 6665). The application places the referred call itself; through this handle it reports that call's progress and final outcome, and the SDK translates each report into a message/sipfrag NOTIFY on the subscription so the transferor sees the real status instead of an optimistic guess. public interface IReferSubscription Remarks Reporting is optional: an accepted REFER already emits an immediate active/100 Trying NOTIFY. If the application never reports, no further NOTIFY is sent and the transferor's subscription lapses at its advertised expiry. The handle is single-shot on termination: the first of ReportSuccess(int, string?) or ReportFailure(int, string?) closes the subscription; all later reports (progress or terminal) are ignored. All members are thread-safe and non-blocking — a report schedules the NOTIFY and returns without awaiting the network. Methods ReportFailure(int, string?) Reports that the referred call failed — a terminated NOTIFY with the sipfrag SIP/2.0 {statusCode} {reasonPhrase} — and closes the subscription. The first terminal report wins; later reports are ignored. void ReportFailure(int statusCode, string? reasonPhrase = null) Parameters statusCode int The final 3xx-6xx status code (e.g. 486 Busy Here). reasonPhrase string Optional reason phrase; a sensible default is used when null. ReportPending() Marks the subscription as pending (RFC 6665 §4.1.3): the transfer was accepted but the referred call has not started yet. Makes the immediate NOTIFY carry Subscription-State: pending instead of active. Only effective when called synchronously inside the transfer handler, before the first NOTIFY is sent; the first subsequent progress report transitions the subscription to active. Ignored once the subscription is already active or terminated. void ReportPending() ReportProgress(int, string?) Reports arbitrary interim progress of the referred call as an active NOTIFY carrying the sipfrag SIP/2.0 {statusCode} {reasonPhrase}. Intended for provisional (1xx) statuses such as 183 Session Progress. Ignored once the subscription has terminated. void ReportProgress(int statusCode, string? reasonPhrase = null) Parameters statusCode int The provisional SIP status code to report. reasonPhrase string Optional reason phrase; a sensible default is used when null. ReportRinging() Reports that the referred call is ringing — an active NOTIFY with the sipfrag SIP/2.0 180 Ringing. Ignored once the subscription has terminated. void ReportRinging() ReportSuccess(int, string?) Reports that the referred call completed successfully — a terminated NOTIFY with the sipfrag SIP/2.0 {statusCode} {reasonPhrase} (default 200 OK) — and closes the subscription. The first terminal report wins; later reports are ignored. void ReportSuccess(int statusCode = 200, string? reasonPhrase = null) Parameters statusCode int The final 2xx status code; defaults to 200. reasonPhrase string Optional reason phrase; a sensible default is used when null. ReportTrying() Reports that the referred call is being tried — an active NOTIFY with the sipfrag SIP/2.0 100 Trying. Ignored once the subscription has terminated. void ReportTrying()

_api/CalloraVoipSdk.Core.Domain.Calls.Ne.title: Enum NetworkQuality | CalloraVoipSdk
_api/CalloraVoipSdk.Core.Domain.Calls.Ne.summary: Enum NetworkQuality Namespace CalloraVoipSdk.Core.Domain.Calls Assembly CalloraVoipSdk.Core.dll Coarse, ready-to-use indicator of the media path's health, derived by the SDK from the congestion signal (delay trend + loss). Meant for a simple UI hint or a plugin decision — read it instead of interpreting raw metrics yourself. _api/CalloraVoipSdk.Core.Domain.Calls.ht.title: Namespace CalloraVoipSdk.Core.Domain.Calls | CalloraVoipSdk
_api/CalloraVoipSdk.Core.Domain.Calls.ht.summary: Namespace CalloraVoipSdk.Core.Domain.Calls Classes CallActionResult Unified result model for extended call control operations. CallIceCandidate Represents one ICE candidate associated with a call media leg. CallIceSnapshot Read-only snapshot of ICE (RFC 8445 / RFC 7675) connectivity establishment for one call media leg. Produced once candidate-pair selection completes and exposed via IceSnapshot. It explains which local/remote candidate pair media flows over and why — otherwise an ICE-driven media path or teardown is opaque to the consumer. Non-ICE calls never produce a snapshot (IceSnapshot stays null). CallMediaParameters Negotiated media parameters for one active call leg. Produced by the infrastructure adapter after SDP offer/answer exchange and consumed by the application media orchestrator to set up RTP I/O. A record so a derived leg (e.g. after ICE candidate-pair selection) can be produced with a with expression that carries every field across — a hand-written copy had silently dropped the SDES/DTLS key material and video parameters when overriding the endpoints. CallTerminationReason Protocol-neutral description of why a call terminated, surfaced on the public call surface. It is populated for both locally and remotely initiated terminations and is readable at (and before) the Terminated state change. SipStatusCode and ReasonPhrase carry the raw SIP detail when the termination came from SIP signaling; Category and TerminatedBy classify it without requiring SIP knowledge. CallVideoParameters Negotiated video parameters for one call leg (WebRTC phase 2). Present on Video only when the SDP exchange negotiated an active video m-line with a codec the SDK supports; null keeps the call audio-only. Grouped into one object so parameter enrichment passes video through as a unit. DialOptions Per-call dialing options — a pure Domain value object supplied to DialAsync(string, DialOptions?, CancellationToken). Structs CallId Strongly-typed, immutable identifier for a single call instance. CallQualitySnapshot Public quality snapshot for one call media leg. Values are updated continuously while the call is active and can be used by SDK consumers for routing, alerting, or UI quality indicators. CallRtpStatistics Raw RTP transport statistics for one active call media leg, exposed for diagnostics, billing and troubleshooting. Unlike CallQualitySnapshot — which surfaces derived quality metrics (jitter/loss in ms/%, MOS) — this record carries the underlying RFC 3550 counters (SSRC identifiers, packet/octet counts, RTP-unit jitter) without interpretation. Available on RtpStatistics once media is flowing. DtmfTone Validated DTMF tone (0-9, *, #, A-D). Interfaces ICall A single call and its lifecycle. IReferSubscription Live handle to the implicit subscription created by an accepted inbound SIP REFER (RFC 3515 / RFC 6665). The application places the referred call itself; through this handle it reports that call's progress and final outcome, and the SDK translates each report into a message/sipfrag NOTIFY on the subscription so the transferor sees the real status instead of an optimistic guess. Enums CallActionStatus Outcome category for extended call control operations. CallDirection Indicates whether a call was initiated by the local party or received from a remote party. CallIceState Public lifecycle state of ICE (RFC 8445) connectivity establishment for one call media leg, surfaced read-only via State. Non-ICE calls never produce an ICE snapshot, so this state is only meaningful when ICE was negotiated for the leg. CallState Lifecycle state of a call. CallTerminatedBy Which side ended the call. CallTerminationCategory Coarse, protocol-neutral classification of why a call ended. Derived from the underlying SIP status (RFC 3261 §21) when the termination came from signaling, but expressed so an application can branch on the outcome without knowing SIP. NetworkQuality Coarse, ready-to-use indicator of the media path's health, derived by the SDK from the congestion signal (delay trend + loss). Meant for a simple UI hint or a plugin decision — read it instead of interpreting raw metrics yourself. A call-media value describing the leg, alongside CallQualitySnapshot.

_api/CalloraVoipSdk.Core.Domain.Lines.IP.summary: Interface IPhoneLine Namespace CalloraVoipSdk.Core.Domain.Lines Assembly CalloraVoipSdk.Core.dll A registered SIP line (account) that places and receives calls. public interface IPhoneLine Remarks All events on this interface are raised on the SDK's SIP signaling/registration thread and run the handler synchronously on it. _api/CalloraVoipSdk.Core.Domain.Lines.Li.title: Enum LineState | CalloraVoipSdk
_api/CalloraVoipSdk.Core.Domain.Lines.Li.summary: Enum LineState Namespace CalloraVoipSdk.Core.Domain.Lines Assembly CalloraVoipSdk.Core.dll Describes the current registration state of a phone line. public enum LineState Fields Failed = 5 Re-registration permanently failed — either MaxRetries was exceeded or the server rejected credentials (401/403). No further attempts will be made. Ready = 6 Operational without a registration: the line never sends REGISTER because Register is false (an IP-authenticated static-IP trunk, where the peer recognises us by source address). Calls can be placed and received. This is a steady state, not a step towards Registered — a line in this mode never reaches that state, and Unregistered would misreport it as unusable. Consumers gating on "line is ready to dial" must accept Registered or this value. Appended at the end of the enum so the existing members keep their numeric values. Reconnecting = 3 A previous registration was lost and the SDK is waiting to retry. Transitions back to Registering before each attempt. Registered = 2 Successfully registered with the SIP registrar. Registering = 1 A registration request is in flight. RegistrationFailed = 4 The most recent registration attempt failed; retry may follow. Unregistered = 0 Not registered; no active SIP binding.

_api/CalloraVoipSdk.Core.Domain.Lines.Si.summary: Class SipAccount Namespace CalloraVoipSdk.Core.Domain.Lines Assembly CalloraVoipSdk.Core.dll Configuration of a SIP account used to register a IPhoneLine and place/receive calls. public sealed class SipAccount Inheritance object SipAccount Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Properties AcceptTrunkInbound Whether the line accepts inbound INVITEs delivered by its registrar/proxy peer or, only when the source is unknown, addressed to its registered domain (SIP-trunk behavior). When true (default) a call for the exact username is always accepted, plus — when no InboundNumbers whitelist is set — calls from the trusted registrar peer and domain-addressed calls from an unknown source. Set to false for a strict 1:1 user account that must accept only its own username. Ignored when InboundNumbers is set (whitelist wins). public bool AcceptTrunkInbound { get; init; } Property Value bool Address The account's SIP address-of-record, derived as sip:Username@SipServer. public SipAddress Address { get; } Property Value SipAddress Credentials The authentication credentials derived from Username and Password. public SipCredentials Credentials { get; } Property Value SipCredentials DisplayName Human-readable caller name shown to the remote party; empty by default. public string DisplayName { get; init; } Property Value string EffectivePort The port actually used: Port when non-zero, otherwise the default for Transport (5060 UDP/TCP, 5061 TLS, 80 WS, 443 WSS). public int EffectivePort { get; } Property Value int InboundNumbers Optional inbound number (DID) whitelist for SIP trunks. When set, the line only accepts inbound INVITEs whose called number (To user-part on the registered domain) is in this list — useful to disambiguate multiple lines on the same provider domain. When null or empty, the line accepts calls for its exact username, calls delivered by the registrar it registered to, and any number on its registered domain (trunk default). Username-only accounts are unaffected. public IReadOnlyList<string>? InboundNumbers { get; init; } Property Value IReadOnlyList<string> Remarks Required when Username is empty. The username is what gives a line its exact 1:1 match; without it the only remaining rule is "anything on this domain", so a line would answer every inbound call the provider sends — including those meant for a different line on the same domain. Connecting such an account is refused rather than silently over-accepting. OutboundProxy Optional outbound proxy to route signaling through instead of resolving SipServer directly. public string? OutboundProxy { get; init; } Property Value string Password SIP account password. Optional: it is only needed when the registrar challenges the registration (401/407). Leave it empty for accounts that do not authenticate — for example an IP-authenticated trunk, or a registrar that does not challenge. If a challenge does arrive and no password is set, registration fails with a clear error. public string Password { get; init; } Property Value string Port Signaling port; 0 (default) selects the standard port for the chosen Transport. public int Port { get; init; } Property Value int Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException The value is outside 0..65535 (#165 P3-11). PublicMediaHost Optional public IP address to force into the SDP media connection line (c=) and RTP bind for calls on this line. By default the media address is auto-resolved from the OS routing table and NAT is handled by symmetric RTP; set this only behind CGNAT / a static 1:1 NAT with port preservation where the peer does not latch to the source address. Must be an IP literal; non-IP values are ignored. null keeps the auto-resolved media address (default, unchanged behavior). public string? PublicMediaHost { get; init; } Property Value string PublicSipHost Optional public host (IP or FQDN) to advertise in the REGISTER Contact and Via sent-by instead of the auto-resolved local address. Required behind NAT for public SIP trunks (e.g. sipgate), whose registrar would otherwise bind the number to an unroutable private LAN address and mark the line offline. null keeps the local address (LAN/direct scenarios). public string? PublicSipHost { get; init; } Property Value string PublicSipPort Optional public signaling port paired with PublicSipHost. Use when a NAT port mapping differs from the local port. null or 0 reuses the local signaling port. public int? PublicSipPort { get; init; } Property Value int? Register Whether the line registers with SipServer. true by default. public bool Register { get; init; } Property Value bool Remarks Set to false for an IP-authenticated static-IP trunk: the provider recognises the customer by source address, no REGISTER is expected, and sending one is at best ignored and at worst rejected. The line then never sends an initial REGISTER, reaches Ready instead of Registered, and places outbound calls straight at SipServer (or OutboundProxy). Not the same as Disabled, which only stops re-registration after a lost binding — the initial REGISTER still goes out there. Inbound still works and is governed by the usual trunk rules (AcceptTrunkInbound, InboundNumbers). RegistrationExpiry and Reregister are ignored in this mode. Note that the mass-market trunks (sipgate, easybell, Telekom CompanyFlex) do register — leave this at the default for those. RegistrationExpiry Requested registration lifetime in seconds; defaults to 300. Ignored when Register is false. public int RegistrationExpiry { get; init; } Property Value int Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException The value is not positive (#165 P3-11). Reregister Controls automatic re-registration when the SIP binding is lost. Defaults to Default (unlimited retries, exponential backoff). public ReregisterOptions Reregister { get; init; } Property Value ReregisterOptions SipServer SIP registrar host (IP or FQDN) and the account's SIP domain (required). public required string SipServer { get; init; } Property Value string Exceptions ArgumentException The value is blank (#165 P3-11). Transport Transport used for SIP signaling; defaults to Udp. public SipTransport Transport { get; init; } Property Value SipTransport Username SIP authentication user and address user-part. Empty by default. public string Username { get; init; } Property Value string Remarks Required in practice for every account that registers — it is the AOR user-part the registrar binds and the name it challenges. Leave it empty only for an IP-authenticated trunk (Register = false) that has no account user at all: addresses then take the host-only form sip:host (RFC 3261 §19.1.1) instead of sip:user@host. Without a user-part there is no 1:1 match for inbound calls, so InboundNumbers becomes the only way to say which calls belong to this line — see the note there.

_api/CalloraVoipSdk.Hosting.ITurnServerH.title: Interface ITurnServerHost | CalloraVoipSdk
_api/CalloraVoipSdk.Hosting.ITurnServerH.summary: Interface ITurnServerHost Namespace CalloraVoipSdk.Hosting Assembly CalloraVoipSdk.Client.dll A hostable TURN relay server (RFC 8656) — the server-side counterpart to the client facades (VoipClient, WebRtcClient). It binds its socket on construction (so LocalEndPoint is known immediately, including after an ephemeral bind), starts serving on Start(), and stops and releases everything on disposal. It serves the TURN methods (Allocate / Refresh / CreatePermission / ChannelBind / Send / Data, plus the TCP extension); it does not answer bare STUN Binding requests — for server-reflexive discovery run an IStunServerHost alongside it. public interface ITurnServerHost : IAsyncDisposable Inherited Members IAsyncDisposable.DisposeAsync() Properties LocalEndPoint The endpoint the server is bound to (the actual port after an ephemeral :0 bind). IPEndPoint LocalEndPoint { get; } Property Value IPEndPoint Methods Start() Starts the server's listen loop. Idempotent — a second call on a started server is a no-op. A start that fails is not committed, so the host stays startable and a retry runs it again; starting a disposed host throws rather than pretending to serve (#166 P3-12). void Start() Exceptions ObjectDisposedException The host has been disposed.

_api/CalloraVoipSdk.Hosting.RecordingEnc.summary: Class RecordingEncryption Namespace CalloraVoipSdk.Hosting Assembly CalloraVoipSdk.Client.dll Factory for the SDK's built-in AES-256-GCM recording encryption. It hands back an IRecordingEncryptionProvider ready to assign to EncryptionProvider, so a consumer can encrypt finalized recording files with the shipped reference implementation without writing their own crypto. public static class RecordingEncryption Inheritance object RecordingEncryption Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Remarks The concrete provider (an AES-GCM-HKDF STREAM construction, constant memory regardless of file size) is an internal Infrastructure implementation detail; this Client-layer facade is the public seam that builds it — the same pattern the SDK uses to expose the built-in TURN/STUN servers (ITurnServerHost, IStunServerHost). Keep the returned provider for the whole recording session and dispose it (via RecordingOptions ownership or directly) so its key is zeroed from memory. using var provider = RecordingEncryption.FromPassphrase("correct horse battery staple", salt); var options = new RecordingOptions { EncryptionProvider = provider }; Methods FromKey(ReadOnlySpan<byte>) Creates a provider from a raw 32-byte AES-256 key. public static IRecordingEncryptionProvider FromKey(ReadOnlySpan<byte> key) Parameters key ReadOnlySpan<byte> The AES-256 key; must be exactly 32 bytes. Interfaces IStunServerHost A hostable STUN server (RFC 5389) for server-reflexive address discovery — the pure-STUN counterpart to ITurnServerHost. It binds its socket on construction (so LocalEndPoint is known immediately, including after an ephemeral bind), answers Binding requests from Start(), and releases everything on disposal. ITurnServerHost A hostable TURN relay server (RFC 8656) — the server-side counterpart to the client facades (VoipClient, WebRtcClient). It binds its socket on construction (so LocalEndPoint is known immediately, including after an ephemeral bind), starts serving on Start(), and stops and releases everything on disposal. It serves the TURN methods (Allocate / Refresh / CreatePermission / ChannelBind / Send / Data, plus the TCP extension); it does not answer bare STUN Binding requests — for server-reflexive discovery run an IStunServerHost alongside it.

Register(IVoipClientModule) Registers one module instance. The OnAttached(IVoipClient) hook runs first; the module only becomes resolvable after the hook completed, so consumers never observe a partially initialized module. When multiple registered modules satisfy the same contract, resolution returns the first registered match. public void Register(IVoipClientModule module) Parameters module IVoipClientModule Remarks Registration closes when the owning client is disposed. The attach hook hands the module the client, and a module attaching to a disposed one would wire itself to torn-down transport, lines and media and then stay registered in a dead owner for its whole lifetime — so a late registration is refused rather than half-performed (#166 P3-13). Resolution keeps working, so a teardown path can still reach its modules. Exceptions ObjectDisposedException The owning client has been disposed. _api/CalloraVoipSdk.VoipConfiguration.ht.title: Class VoipConfiguration | CalloraVoipSdk
_api/CalloraVoipSdk.VoipConfiguration.ht.summary: Class VoipConfiguration Namespace CalloraVoipSdk Assembly CalloraVoipSdk.Client.dll Top-level SDK configuration: identity, transport security, logging, media/codec behavior, and call-lifecycle timeouts. Supplied once when constructing or registering the SDK. public sealed class VoipConfiguration Inheritance object VoipConfiguration Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Properties AudioDevice Audio device to use for all calls. If left at SilenceAudioDevice and auto selection is enabled, the SDK attempts to load a platform device (Linux/Windows) at runtime. public IAudioDevice AudioDevice { get; init; } Property Value IAudioDevice BridgeAudioFormat Audio format delivered to and expected from the media consumer (bridge/tap). When set to Pcmu, the SDK transcodes between the negotiated wire codec (e.g. Opus) and G.711 µ-law so a µ-law-only consumer works over any negotiated codec. Default Passthrough delivers the raw wire payload. public BridgeAudioFormat BridgeAudioFormat { get; init; } Property Value BridgeAudioFormat DefaultTransport Default SIP signaling transport for outbound requests and the advertised local contact when a target URI does not force one. Defaults to Udp, preserving the prior behavior; set to Tcp/Tls/etc. for TCP- or TLS-only enterprise proxies. public SipTransport DefaultTransport { get; init; } Property Value SipTransport DtlsCertificate Optional DTLS-SRTP identity certificate (RFC 5763) for the media plane. null (default) generates a fresh ephemeral ECDSA P-256 certificate per client instance — the WebRTC privacy default. Supply your own for a stable/pinned identity (enterprise, compliance): it must be an ECDSA P-256 certificate with an accessible private key (RSA, other curves, and non-exportable HSM keys are rejected fail-closed). The DTLS certificate is authenticated by SDP a=fingerprint (RFC 8122), not PKI, and is independent of the SIP-TLS certificate (Tls) — pass the same X509Certificate2 to both to share one identity. public X509Certificate2? DtlsCertificate { get; init; } Property Value X509Certificate2 EnableAutomaticAudioDeviceSelection Automatically load a platform audio device when AudioDevice is left at CalloraVoipSdk.Core.Infrastructure.Audio.SilenceAudioDevice. public bool EnableAutomaticAudioDeviceSelection { get; init; } Property Value bool EnableVideo When true, calls negotiate a video stream (WebRTC phase 2, RFC 6184/7741): offers carry an m=video line and inbound video offers are answered. Encoded video frames are exchanged via ICall's media session; the SDK does not encode/decode video itself. Default: false (audio-only). Video is offered only when the offer is not SDES-keyed: an outbound offer under a SDES-offering SrtpPolicy (Optional/Required without OfferDtlsSrtp) stays audio-only — offer DTLS-SRTP or run plain to carry video. Inbound plain/DTLS video offers are answered regardless; SDES video is declined until per-m-line video keying lands. Note: video does not yet gather ICE candidates — with Ice enabled the video m-line carries its port but no candidates, so video needs direct connectivity (no ICE-only peer) until per-component video ICE lands. public bool EnableVideo { get; init; } Property Value bool HangupHeldCallOnMediaSilence Whether the liveness timeout also applies to on-hold calls (which legitimately carry no inbound media). Default: false (held calls are not torn down). public bool HangupHeldCallOnMediaSilence { get; init; } Property Value bool Ice ICE runtime configuration for NAT traversal and candidate-pair selection. Disabled by default. public IceConfiguration Ice { get; init; } Property Value IceConfiguration InboundMediaTimeout Hang up a connected call that has shown no sign of life this long — neither inbound RTP nor inbound RTCP. Zero (the default) disables the hangup: media silence is reported through ICall.MediaFlowChanged and the application decides what to do about it. 30 seconds is the recommended value if you want the SDK to end such calls itself. public TimeSpan InboundMediaTimeout { get; init; } Property Value TimeSpan Remarks Off by default because the teardown is a heuristic and the measurement says so (#261, ADR-069): with a PBX in the media path — verified against both Asterisk and FreeSWITCH — inbound RTCP stops together with the media, so nothing on the wire distinguishes "the peer went quiet" (silence suppression per RFC 3389, hold, a bridge switch during a transfer) from "the peer went away". Asterisk (rtp_timeout) and FreeSWITCH (media_timeout) ship theirs disabled for the same reason. A peer that is genuinely gone is still caught by the RFC 4028 session timer. When you do enable it, inbound RTCP counts as a sign of life alongside RTP — it can only extend the deadline, never shorten it — and held calls stay exempt unless HangupHeldCallOnMediaSilence is set. LocalSipPort Local port the SIP listener binds for UDP and TCP. 0 (default) takes an ephemeral port. public int LocalSipPort { get; init; } Property Value int Remarks Leave this at the default for registering accounts: the registrar learns where to reach you from the REGISTER Contact, so the port need not be fixed or known in advance. Set it — normally to 5060 — when nobody tells the peer your address: an IP-authenticated trunk (Register = false) sends no REGISTER, so the provider delivers inbound calls to a pre-agreed address. A fixed port is equally required for static firewall or NAT rules, which an ephemeral port would invalidate on every restart. Binding a port already in use fails at client construction with a SocketException rather than silently landing elsewhere — a listener on the wrong port looks healthy while every inbound call goes missing. LocalSipTlsPort Local port the SIP TLS listener binds. 0 (default) takes an ephemeral port; the SIP convention is 5061 beside 5060 (RFC 3261 §19.1.2). Separate from LocalSipPort because TLS is a second TCP listener and cannot share that port. Only relevant when TLS is configured. public int LocalSipTlsPort { get; init; } Property Value int LoggerFactory Logger factory the SDK logs through; null disables SDK logging. public ILoggerFactory? LoggerFactory { get; init; } Property Value ILoggerFactory MaxConcurrentCallsPerLine Maximum simultaneous calls per phone line. 0 = unlimited. public int MaxConcurrentCallsPerLine { get; init; } Property Value int MediaSilenceNotifyAfter Report inbound media silence through ICall.MediaFlowChanged after this long without inbound RTP — a notification, never a teardown. Zero disables the notification. Default: 15 seconds. public TimeSpan MediaSilenceNotifyAfter { get; init; } Property Value TimeSpan OfferDtlsSrtp When true, outbound call offers advertise DTLS-SRTP keying (RFC 5763: UDP/TLS/RTP/SAVPF profile plus certificate fingerprint) instead of SDES a=crypto. Inbound DTLS-SRTP offers are answered regardless of this setting. Default: false (SDES per SrtpPolicy). public bool OfferDtlsSrtp { get; init; } Property Value bool PreferredAudioCodecs Ordered audio codec preference by SDP encoding name ("PCMU", "PCMA", "G722", "opus"). When set, SDP offers and answers only include the listed codecs (plus DTMF telephone-event) in this order, and RTP sessions use this preference to pick the primary codec. Opus (RFC 7587, 48 kHz) is opt-in: it is only offered/answered when listed here. Unknown names are ignored; when nothing matches, the SDK default set (G722, PCMA, PCMU) is used. When a listed codec is known but the peer does not offer it, negotiation fails rather than producing an audio-less answer. null keeps defaults. public IReadOnlyList<string>? PreferredAudioCodecs { get; init; } Property Value IReadOnlyList<string> PreferredVideoCodecs Ordered video codec preference by SDP encoding name (VP8, H264) when EnableVideo is set. null uses the SDK default (VP8, then H264). Unknown names are ignored. public IReadOnlyList<string>? PreferredVideoCodecs { get; init; } Property Value IReadOnlyList<string> RequireSecureSignalingForSdes Opt-in hard enforcement of the RFC 4568 §7 caveat (see SrtpPolicy). When true, an outbound call that would key SDES over an insecure signaling transport (no TLS/SIPS, and OfferDtlsSrtp unset) is refused (fail-closed) instead of placed with the master key in cleartext SDP. Default: false — such calls proceed but the SDK logs a warning. Set this when a non-confidential media key must never leave the host; use TLS/SIPS signaling or DTLS-SRTP to place calls under this policy. public bool RequireSecureSignalingForSdes { get; init; } Property Value bool SipSignalingHardening Resource limits for the SIP signaling layer: concurrent inbound session caps (global and per-remote), the un-answered ring deadline, and the inbound server-transaction table bounds (#158 P1-5/P1-7). The defaults match the SDK's built-in limits. public SipSignalingHardeningConfiguration SipSignalingHardening { get; init; } Property Value SipSignalingHardeningConfiguration SipTransportHardening Admission and slowloris limits for the inbound SIP listener (connection-oriented transports). Bounds how many inbound connections a peer can pin and how long a handshake may stall (#158 P1-3/P1-4). The defaults match the SDK's built-in limits. public SipTransportHardeningConfiguration SipTransportHardening { get; init; } Property Value SipTransportHardeningConfiguration SrtpPolicy Default media-encryption policy for calls; defaults to Optional. Overridable per call via DialOptions.UseSrtp. Security note (RFC 4568 §7): unless OfferDtlsSrtp is set, SRTP is keyed via SDES, which carries the master key as an a=crypto line inside the SDP. That key is only confidential when the signaling transport is secure (TLS/SIPS). Over UDP/TCP the key travels in cleartext, so a passive eavesdropper on the signaling path can decrypt the media — the SDK logs a warning in this case. For real media confidentiality use TLS/SIPS signaling or enable OfferDtlsSrtp (keys never appear in the SDP). public SrtpPolicy SrtpPolicy { get; init; } Property Value SrtpPolicy Tls TLS settings for secure SIP transport; null uses the transport defaults. public TlsConfiguration? Tls { get; init; } Property Value TlsConfiguration UserAgent Value sent in the SIP User-Agent header; defaults to CalloraVoipSdk/1.0. public string UserAgent { get; init; } Property Value string

_api/CalloraVoipSdk.WebRtc.IAudioTrack.h.summary: Interface IAudioTrack Namespace CalloraVoipSdk.WebRtc Assembly CalloraVoipSdk.Client.dll A handle to an outbound audio track added with AddAudioTrack() (its own m=audio line on the shared BUNDLE transport, beyond the peer's primary audio anchor). Send encoded audio payloads on this track with SendFrameAsync(ReadOnlyMemory<byte>, uint, CancellationToken); each track carries its own SSRC, so payloads sent on distinct handles never collide (RFC 3550 §8.1). The SFU pattern of one audio stream per remote participant on a single peer connection. public interface IAudioTrack Remarks Adding a track supplements the peer's implicit primary audio track (the always-on transport anchor that SendAudioAsync(ReadOnlyMemory<byte>, CancellationToken) addresses); the frameless SendAudioAsync(ReadOnlyMemory<byte>, CancellationToken) keeps addressing that primary track. A track added before CreateOffer() is negotiated in the first offer; a track added mid-call is pending until the next offer/answer cycle applies it to the live session (RFC 8829 renegotiation). Audio has no simulcast, so there is no per-layer send overload. DTMF (RFC 4733) stays on the primary audio track and is not surfaced per additional track — send it via SendDtmfAsync(byte, int, CancellationToken). Properties Direction The direction this track was added with (RFC 3264). TrackDirection Direction { get; } Property Value TrackDirection Mid The track's negotiated MID (a=mid, RFC 5888) — a numeric token on the multi-track transport. string Mid { get; } Property Value string Methods SendFrameAsync(ReadOnlyMemory<byte>, uint, CancellationToken) Sends one already-encoded audio RTP payload on this track, with rtpTimestamp set on the outbound RTP packets (RFC 3550 §5.1). The app owns the codec (transport-only). The timestamp is stamped on the wire — not derived from an internal cursor — so an SFU forwarding this stream preserves the source's timestamp for A/V-sync against forwarded video; the app supplies the source's own RTP timestamp per payload. Suppressed until the DTLS handshake keys the transport; a no-op when the negotiated directions do not carry outbound audio on this track (a send-only/inactive remote answer, or a recv-only/inactive local side, RFC 3264). Task SendFrameAsync(ReadOnlyMemory<byte> encodedAudioFrame, uint rtpTimestamp, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Parameters encodedAudioFrame ReadOnlyMemory<byte> The already-encoded audio RTP payload. rtpTimestamp uint The payload's RTP timestamp on the track's negotiated audio clock; stamped on the outbound packets. cancellationToken CancellationToken Cancels the send. Returns Task

_api/CalloraVoipSdk.WebRtc.IEncodedMedia.summary: Interface IEncodedMediaSink Namespace CalloraVoipSdk.WebRtc Assembly CalloraVoipSdk.Client.dll A destination for recorded encoded media. The recorder writes every captured RecordedFrame here (both directions, audio and video); the sink decides how to persist it — a per-track file, a container, an upload, an in-memory buffer, … Transport-only: payloads are the raw codec bitstream (no decoding). A container writer (Opus→Ogg, VP8→IVF, muxed MP4/…) is a concrete sink implementation. public interface IEncodedMediaSink Remarks Write(in RecordedFrame) is invoked on the media path — it must return quickly and should not throw (a throwing sink is isolated from the media flow and its frame is dropped). CompleteAsync(CancellationToken) is invoked exactly once when the recording stops, to flush and finalise. Methods CompleteAsync(CancellationToken) Flushes and finalises the sink; called once when recording stops. ValueTask CompleteAsync(CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Parameters cancellationToken CancellationToken Returns ValueTask Write(in RecordedFrame) Persists one captured frame. void Write(in RecordedFrame frame) Parameters frame RecordedFrame

_api/CalloraVoipSdk.WebRtc.IMediaTap.htm.title: Interface IMediaTap | CalloraVoipSdk
_api/CalloraVoipSdk.WebRtc.IMediaTap.htm.summary: Interface IMediaTap Namespace CalloraVoipSdk.WebRtc Assembly CalloraVoipSdk.Client.dll An L3 observer of the encoded media flowing through an IPeerConnection in both directions — the extension seam for recording, analytics, or feeding an AI pipeline without owning the peer. Attach with AttachMediaTap(IMediaTap) and dispose the handle to detach. public interface IMediaTap Remarks Transport-only: payloads are the raw depacketised codec bitstream. A tap is invoked on the media path, so it must return quickly and should not throw — a throwing tap is caught, logged, and isolated from the media flow rather than being allowed to break it. Methods OnAudio(MediaDirection, ReadOnlyMemory<byte>) Observes one audio payload in the given direction. void OnAudio(MediaDirection direction, ReadOnlyMemory<byte> payload) Parameters direction MediaDirection payload ReadOnlyMemory<byte> OnVideo(MediaDirection, ReadOnlyMemory<byte>, uint?, bool, string?) Observes one video frame in the given direction. rtpTimestamp is null when unknown; isKeyFrame is false for outbound frames (the send path does not carry the flag). rid is the simulcast layer id (RFC 8853) for an outbound simulcast frame, so a tap can tell the layers apart; it is null for a single-stream send and for inbound frames (receive-side RID demux is a later slice). Richer per-frame metadata (MID/SSRC/track ids) will follow when those are surfaced. void OnVideo(MediaDirection direction, ReadOnlyMemory<byte> frame, uint? rtpTimestamp, bool isKeyFrame, string? rid) Parameters direction MediaDirection frame ReadOnlyMemory<byte> rtpTimestamp uint? isKeyFrame bool rid string

_api/CalloraVoipSdk.WebRtc.IPeerConnecti.title: Interface IPeerConnection | CalloraVoipSdk
_api/CalloraVoipSdk.WebRtc.IPeerConnecti.summary: Interface IPeerConnection Namespace CalloraVoipSdk.WebRtc Assembly CalloraVoipSdk.Client.dll A signalling-neutral WebRTC peer connection: the app owns the signalling channel (WebSocket/HTTP/ Callora) and exchanges SDP through it, while this peer runs ICE, DTLS-SRTP, BUNDLE and the RTP/RTCP transport. Encoded media flows through SendAudioAsync(ReadOnlyMemory<byte>, CancellationToken)/SendVideoFrameAsync(ReadOnlyMemory<byte>, uint, CancellationToken) — the SDK is transport-only, so the app owns the codec. The central per-connection abstraction of the WebRTC facade, mirroring the SIP ICall. public interface IPeerConnection : IAsyncDisposable Inherited Members IAsyncDisposable.DisposeAsync() Extension Methods WebRtcPeerConnectionExtensions.ConnectAsync(IPeerConnection, IWebRtcSignaling, WebRtcRole, CancellationToken) Properties LocalDescription The local SDP (offer or answer) once one has been produced; null before. string? LocalDescription { get; } Property Value string LocalMediaEndPoint The bound local media endpoint once the transport has bound; null before. IPEndPoint? LocalMediaEndPoint { get; } Property Value IPEndPoint RecommendedOutgoingBitrateBps The SDK's current recommended outbound send bitrate to this peer in bits per second (transport-cc, draft-holmer-rmcat-transport-wide-cc-extensions-01 — not RFC 8888 CCFB, see the codec remarks), for setting the encoder or — for an SFU — selecting which simulcast layer to forward to this receiver. null until a media session is running and transport-cc has been negotiated for this leg. The point-in-time counterpart to RecommendedBitrateChanged; the same value the last event carried. long? RecommendedOutgoingBitrateBps { get; } Property Value long? SignalingState The current RFC 8829 §4.1.3 signalling state — the offer/answer half of the peer's lifecycle, distinct from the ICE/DTLS transport State. Starts at Stable and settles back there once each offer/answer exchange completes; see SignalingState for the transitions this SDK models. Mirrors the W3C RTCPeerConnection.signalingState. SignalingState SignalingState { get; } Property Value SignalingState State Current lifecycle state (RFC 8829). PeerConnectionState State { get; } Property Value PeerConnectionState Methods AddAudioTrack() Adds an audio track (its own m=audio line on the shared BUNDLE transport, beyond the primary audio anchor) before the first offer, returning a handle to send payloads on it. The happy path: var extra = peer.AddAudioTrack(); await extra.SendFrameAsync(payload, ts);. The SFU pattern of one audio stream per remote participant on a single peer connection. IAudioTrack AddAudioTrack() Returns IAudioTrack A handle to send encoded audio payloads on the new track. Remarks The peer's implicit primary audio track stays the always-on transport anchor; AddAudioTrack adds a further audio m-line. The frameless SendAudioAsync(ReadOnlyMemory<byte>, CancellationToken) keeps addressing the primary track, and DTMF (SendDtmfAsync(byte, int, CancellationToken), RFC 4733) stays on that primary track. A track added before CreateOffer() is negotiated in the first offer; a track added mid-call is pending until the next offer/answer cycle applies it to the running session (RFC 8829 renegotiation). Throws only after the peer is closed. Exceptions InvalidOperationException The peer is closed. AddAudioTrack(AudioTrackOptions) Adds an audio track with deeper control — direction, codecs, and the MediaStream it belongs to (see AudioTrackOptions) — before the first offer. See AddAudioTrack() for the primary-anchor semantics and the mid-call renegotiation behaviour. IAudioTrack AddAudioTrack(AudioTrackOptions options) Parameters options AudioTrackOptions The track's direction, codecs, and stream id. Returns IAudioTrack A handle to send encoded audio payloads on the new track. Exceptions InvalidOperationException The peer is closed. AddIceCandidateAsync(string, CancellationToken) Applies a remote ICE candidate that trickled in out-of-band (RFC 8838), as an RFC 8829 candidate: line. The highest-priority component-1 UDP candidate becomes the send target; a malformed or unusable candidate is ignored. Task AddIceCandidateAsync(string candidate, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Parameters candidate string cancellationToken CancellationToken Returns Task AddVideoTrack() Adds a video track (its own m=video line on the shared BUNDLE transport), returning a handle to send frames on it. The happy path: var cam = peer.AddVideoTrack(); await cam.SendFrameAsync(frame, ts);. IVideoTrack AddVideoTrack() Returns IVideoTrack A handle to send encoded frames on the new track. Remarks Backward-compatible semantics: EnableVideo stays the implicit primary video track (unchanged SDP); AddVideoTrack adds a further track (or the first, when EnableVideo is false). The frameless SendVideoFrameAsync(ReadOnlyMemory<byte>, uint, CancellationToken) keeps addressing the primary track. A track added before the first offer is negotiated in that offer; a track added mid-call is pending until the next CreateOffer()/SetRemoteDescriptionAsync(string, CancellationToken) cycle applies it to the running session (RFC 8829 renegotiation). Exceptions InvalidOperationException The peer is closed. AddVideoTrack(VideoTrackOptions) Adds a video track with deeper control — direction, codecs, send-side simulcast layers, and the MediaStream it belongs to (see VideoTrackOptions). See AddVideoTrack() for the backward-compatibility and mid-call renegotiation semantics. IVideoTrack AddVideoTrack(VideoTrackOptions options) Parameters options VideoTrackOptions The track's direction, codecs, simulcast layers, and stream id. Returns IVideoTrack A handle to send encoded frames on the new track. Exceptions InvalidOperationException The peer is closed. AttachMediaTap(IMediaTap) Attaches an IMediaTap that observes the encoded media flowing through this peer in both directions (L3 recording/analytics/AI seam). Dispose the returned handle to detach. IDisposable AttachMediaTap(IMediaTap tap) Parameters tap IMediaTap Returns IDisposable CreateOffer() Produces a local WebRTC offer (BUNDLE, DTLS-SRTP, ICE, rtcp-mux) for the app to signal out. string CreateOffer() Returns string GatherCandidatesAsync(CancellationToken) Gathers server-reflexive ICE candidates (RFC 8445 §5.1.1) from the configured STUN servers, each surfaced on LocalIceCandidateDiscovered to trickle out (RFC 8838). No-op when no STUN servers are configured. Call after producing the offer/answer and before StartAsync(CancellationToken) (the query shares the media socket the transport takes over once started; calling it after StartAsync(CancellationToken) throws). On loopback (the STUN server on the same host) the reflexive address equals the host candidate; redundant-candidate pruning (RFC 8445 §5.4) is a later slice. Task GatherCandidatesAsync(CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Parameters cancellationToken CancellationToken Returns Task GetStats() Takes a statistics snapshot for this peer (the SDK's getStats). Bitrates are derived per call, so poll periodically (e.g. once per second) for meaningful rate values. WebRtcStats GetStats() Returns WebRtcStats RequestVideoKeyFrameAsync(string, CancellationToken) Asks the peer to send a fresh video key frame on the track identified by mid (RFC 4585 §6.3.1 PLI) — the multi-track overload of RequestVideoKeyFrameAsync(CancellationToken). Use it when the bundle carries several video tracks and only one needs an intra frame (a renderer attach or a decoder reset on that track). Tolerant by design — a no-op returning false when no BUNDLE session is negotiated yet, no track carries that MID, the peer did not advertise PLI (a=rtcp-fb … nack pli), or the built-in throttle still holds; returns true when a PLI was sent. Safe to call from any thread and after disposal (a no-op). ValueTask<bool> RequestVideoKeyFrameAsync(string mid, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Parameters mid string The media identification (a=mid) of the video track to request a key frame for. cancellationToken CancellationToken Cancels the RTCP send. Returns ValueTask<bool> true when a PLI was sent to the peer; otherwise false. Exceptions ArgumentException mid is null or empty. RequestVideoKeyFrameAsync(CancellationToken) Asks the peer to send a fresh video key frame (RFC 4585 §6.3.1 PLI). This is the receiving side's counterpart to VideoKeyFrameRequested: call it when a newly attached renderer or a decoder reset needs an intra frame to start/recover decoding, independent of automatic loss-driven feedback. Tolerant by design — a no-op returning false when no BUNDLE session is negotiated yet, the bundle has no video track, the peer did not advertise PLI (a=rtcp-fb … nack pli), or the built-in 500 ms throttle still holds; returns true when a PLI was sent. Safe to call from any thread and after disposal (a no-op). ValueTask<bool> RequestVideoKeyFrameAsync(CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Parameters cancellationToken CancellationToken Cancels the RTCP send. Returns ValueTask<bool> true when a PLI was sent to the peer; otherwise false. SendAudioAsync(ReadOnlyMemory<byte>, CancellationToken) Sends one already-encoded audio RTP payload on the peer's audio track. A no-op when the negotiated directions do not carry outbound audio from this peer (a send-only/inactive remote answer, or a recv-only/inactive local side, RFC 3264): the audio m-line still anchors the transport and inbound audio is still received, but nothing is streamed to a remote that will not receive it. ValueTask SendAudioAsync(ReadOnlyMemory<byte> payload, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Parameters payload ReadOnlyMemory<byte> cancellationToken CancellationToken Returns ValueTask SendDtmfAsync(byte, int, CancellationToken) Sends one out-of-band DTMF tone (RFC 4733 telephone-event) on the peer's audio track. A no-op is not possible: telephone-event must have been negotiated, otherwise this throws. The tone is streamed as an event burst on the audio stream's RTP clock, suppressed until the DTLS handshake keys the transport. Task SendDtmfAsync(byte toneCode, int durationMs = 160, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Parameters toneCode byte The DTMF event code (0–9, 10=*, 11=#, 12–15=A–D per RFC 4733 §3.2). durationMs int The tone duration in milliseconds (default 160; at least the RFC 4733 floor). cancellationToken CancellationToken Cancels the send. Returns Task Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException The tone code exceeds 15, or the duration is below the floor. InvalidOperationException No media session yet, or telephone-event was not negotiated. SendVideoFrameAsync(ReadOnlyMemory<byte>, uint, bool, CancellationToken) Sends one encoded video frame and declares whether it is a key frame, so the SDK can put that fact in the RTP header as a Dependency Descriptor (#225) instead of leaving a receiver to parse it out of the payload. Task SendVideoFrameAsync(ReadOnlyMemory<byte> encodedFrame, uint rtpTimestamp, bool isKeyFrame, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Parameters encodedFrame ReadOnlyMemory<byte> The encoded frame. rtpTimestamp uint The frame's RTP timestamp (RFC 3550 §5.1). isKeyFrame bool Whether the frame can be decoded on its own. cancellationToken CancellationToken Cancels the send. Returns Task Remarks Use this whenever you know — you always do, since you encoded the frame — and especially with OpaqueVideoFrames: an encrypted payload carries no readable key-frame signal at all, so without this the information is simply lost. The descriptor is written only when the peer negotiated the extension; otherwise this behaves exactly like the overload without the flag. SendVideoFrameAsync(ReadOnlyMemory<byte>, uint, CancellationToken) Packetises and sends one already-encoded video frame on the peer's video track. Task SendVideoFrameAsync(ReadOnlyMemory<byte> encodedFrame, uint rtpTimestamp, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Parameters encodedFrame ReadOnlyMemory<byte> rtpTimestamp uint cancellationToken CancellationToken Returns Task SendVideoFrameAsync(string, ReadOnlyMemory<byte>, uint, bool, CancellationToken) Sends one encoded video frame on a simulcast rid layer (RFC 8853) and declares whether it is a key frame — the per-layer counterpart to SendVideoFrameAsync(ReadOnlyMemory<byte>, uint, bool, CancellationToken). Each layer numbers its frames independently, as they are independent RTP streams. Task SendVideoFrameAsync(string rid, ReadOnlyMemory<byte> encodedFrame, uint rtpTimestamp, bool isKeyFrame, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Parameters rid string The simulcast layer's a=rid id. encodedFrame ReadOnlyMemory<byte> The encoded frame. rtpTimestamp uint The frame's RTP timestamp (RFC 3550 §5.1). isKeyFrame bool Whether the frame can be decoded on its own. cancellationToken CancellationToken Cancels the send. Returns Task SendVideoFrameAsync(string, ReadOnlyMemory<byte>, uint, CancellationToken) Packetises and sends one already-encoded video frame on a simulcast rid layer (RFC 8853). The layer must be one of the configured simulcast rids; the app encodes each layer at its own resolution/bitrate and calls this once per layer per frame. Task SendVideoFrameAsync(string rid, ReadOnlyMemory<byte> encodedFrame, uint rtpTimestamp, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Parameters rid string encodedFrame ReadOnlyMemory<byte> rtpTimestamp uint cancellationToken CancellationToken Returns Task SetRemoteDescriptionAsync(string, CancellationToken) Applies a remote SDP. When this peer is the answerer, returns the local answer SDP to signal back; when it is the offerer applying the peer's answer, returns the local offer unchanged. Task<string> SetRemoteDescriptionAsync(string remoteSdp, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Parameters remoteSdp string cancellationToken CancellationToken Returns Task<string> StartAsync(CancellationToken) Starts the media transport (ICE connectivity, DTLS handshake, receive loop). Task StartAsync(CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Parameters cancellationToken CancellationToken Returns Task Events ConnectionStateChanged Raised on every lifecycle transition (RFC 8829 connectionstatechange). event EventHandler<PeerConnectionState>? ConnectionStateChanged Event Type EventHandler<PeerConnectionState> DtmfReceived Raised once per fully received inbound DTMF tone (RFC 4733 telephone-event). Carries the decoded tone and duration; DTMF is not surfaced as audio on the remote audio track. Only fires when the negotiation included telephone-event. event EventHandler<DtmfTone>? DtmfReceived Event Type EventHandler<DtmfTone> LocalIceCandidateDiscovered Raised as each local ICE candidate is gathered (RFC 8838 trickle), carrying the RFC 8829 candidate: line so the app can signal it to the peer out-of-band. Pair with AddIceCandidateAsync(string, CancellationToken) on the remote side. The host candidate is surfaced at offer/answer time; server-reflexive candidates follow from GatherCandidatesAsync(CancellationToken) when STUN servers are configured. event EventHandler<string>? LocalIceCandidateDiscovered Event Type EventHandler<string> RecommendedBitrateChanged Raised whenever the SDK revises its recommended send bitrate to this peer (transport-cc), carrying the finished BitrateRecommendation (bitrate + coarse quality). This is the reactive signal an SFU reacts to per receiver, re-choosing the simulcast layer it forwards when the path's bandwidth changes. Reactive per feedback report (roughly once per round-trip); the SDK does not throttle it — the app decides when and how to act on a change. Stays silent when transport-cc was not negotiated (and RecommendedOutgoingBitrateBps reads null). event EventHandler<BitrateRecommendation>? RecommendedBitrateChanged Event Type EventHandler<BitrateRecommendation> SignalingStateChanged Raised on every RFC 8829 §4.1.3 signalling-state transition (the W3C signalingstatechange), carrying the new SignalingState. The answerer path fires twice in one SetRemoteDescriptionAsync(string, CancellationToken) call — once for HaveRemoteOffer and once for the return to Stable. event EventHandler<SignalingState>? SignalingStateChanged Event Type EventHandler<SignalingState> TrackReceived Raised once per remote track, when that track's first frame arrives (the W3C track event). Subscribe to the track's FrameReceived synchronously in the handler to receive every frame — the first frame is delivered immediately after this event returns. event EventHandler<RemoteTrack>? TrackReceived Event Type EventHandler<RemoteTrack> VideoKeyFrameRequested Raised when the remote peer requests a key frame via an inbound PLI/FIR (RFC 4585/5104). This targets the local encoder — the app should encode and send a key frame so the peer can recover its video. event EventHandler? VideoKeyFrameRequested Event Type EventHandler

_api/CalloraVoipSdk.WebRtc.IVideoTrack.h.summary: Interface IVideoTrack Namespace CalloraVoipSdk.WebRtc Assembly CalloraVoipSdk.Client.dll A handle to an outbound video track added before the first offer with AddVideoTrack() (its own m=video line on the shared BUNDLE transport). Send encoded frames on this track with SendFrameAsync(ReadOnlyMemory<byte>, uint, CancellationToken); each track carries its own SSRC, so frames sent on distinct handles never collide (RFC 3550 §8.1). public interface IVideoTrack Remarks The multi-track surface is preview-grade: tracks must be added before CreateOffer() (mid-call add / renegotiation is a later package). Adding a track supplements the implicit primary video track that EnableVideo enables; the frameless SendVideoFrameAsync(ReadOnlyMemory<byte>, uint, CancellationToken) keeps addressing that primary track. Properties Direction The direction this track was added with (RFC 3264). TrackDirection Direction { get; } Property Value TrackDirection Mid The track's negotiated MID (a=mid, RFC 5888) — a numeric token on the multi-track transport. string Mid { get; } Property Value string Methods SendFrameAsync(ReadOnlyMemory<byte>, uint, CancellationToken) Packetises and sends one already-encoded video frame on this track. The app owns the codec (transport-only). Suppressed until the DTLS handshake keys the transport; a no-op when the negotiated directions do not carry outbound video on this track. Task SendFrameAsync(ReadOnlyMemory<byte> encodedFrame, uint rtpTimestamp, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Parameters encodedFrame ReadOnlyMemory<byte> The already-encoded video frame payload. rtpTimestamp uint The frame's RTP timestamp on the track's 90 kHz clock. cancellationToken CancellationToken Cancels the send. Returns Task SendFrameAsync(string, ReadOnlyMemory<byte>, uint, CancellationToken) Packetises and sends one already-encoded video frame on this track's simulcast rid layer (RFC 8853). The layer must be one of the track's configured SimulcastSendRids; the app encodes each layer at its own resolution/bitrate and calls this once per layer per frame. Task SendFrameAsync(string rid, ReadOnlyMemory<byte> encodedFrame, uint rtpTimestamp, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Parameters rid string The simulcast layer id to send on. encodedFrame ReadOnlyMemory<byte> The already-encoded video frame payload for that layer. rtpTimestamp uint The frame's RTP timestamp on the track's 90 kHz clock. cancellationToken CancellationToken Cancels the send. Returns Task

_api/CalloraVoipSdk.WebRtc.IWebRtcClient.title: Interface IWebRtcClient | CalloraVoipSdk
_api/CalloraVoipSdk.WebRtc.IWebRtcClient.summary: Interface IWebRtcClient Namespace CalloraVoipSdk.WebRtc Assembly CalloraVoipSdk.Client.dll The WebRTC peer facade — the happy-path entry point for building signalling-neutral peer connections. Mirrors the SIP IVoipClient; the advanced peer-registry manager tier is added in a later slice (ADR-012). Disposing the client asynchronously closes every peer it still tracks. Peer teardown is inherently asynchronous (IPeerConnection is IAsyncDisposable), so the client is async-disposable only; a DI host disposes it on the async path (an IHost, or an explicit await using / DisposeAsync on a manually built provider). public interface IWebRtcClient : IAsyncDisposable Inherited Members IAsyncDisposable.DisposeAsync() Properties Modules The registry of optional facade extensions contributed by separate packages (L3 plugin seam); register modules programmatically via Register(IWebRtcClientModule), or register IWebRtcClientModule services before AddCalloraWebRtc to have them auto-attached. IWebRtcModuleRegistry Modules { get; } Property Value IWebRtcModuleRegistry Peers The registry of peer connections currently open on this client (L2 multi-peer manager). IPeerConnectionManager Peers { get; } Property Value IPeerConnectionManager Methods CreatePeer() Creates a new peer connection with the client's configured codecs, DTLS identity and local endpoint. The caller drives signalling and disposes the returned peer. IPeerConnection CreatePeer() Returns IPeerConnection

_api/CalloraVoipSdk.WebRtc.IWebRtcTrickl.title: Interface IWebRtcTrickleSignaling | CalloraVoipSdk
_api/CalloraVoipSdk.WebRtc.IWebRtcTrickl.summary: Interface IWebRtcTrickleSignaling Namespace CalloraVoipSdk.WebRtc Assembly CalloraVoipSdk.Client.dll Extends IWebRtcSignaling with out-of-band ICE candidate trickle (RFC 8838): alongside the offer/answer, the SDK sends each locally gathered candidate as it is discovered and applies remote candidates as they arrive, rather than relying only on the candidates the SDP carried. When an app supplies this on ConnectAsync(IPeerConnection, IWebRtcSignaling, WebRtcRole, CancellationToken), the SDK gathers server-reflexive candidates and runs the trickle exchange; a plain IWebRtcSignaling stays SDP-only. Candidate strings are RFC 8829 candidate:… lines — the wire form browsers exchange verbatim, so no conversion is needed at the app boundary. public interface IWebRtcTrickleSignaling : IWebRtcSignaling Inherited Members IWebRtcSignaling.SendDescriptionAsync(string, CancellationToken) IWebRtcSignaling.ReceiveDescriptionAsync(CancellationToken) Methods ReceiveCandidateAsync(CancellationToken) Awaits the next remote ICE candidate line, or null when the remote has signalled end-of-candidates (RFC 8840) — after which the SDK stops polling for more. _api/CalloraVoipSdk.WebRtc.SignalingStat.title: Enum SignalingState | CalloraVoipSdk
_api/CalloraVoipSdk.WebRtc.SignalingStat.summary: Enum SignalingState Namespace CalloraVoipSdk.WebRtc Assembly CalloraVoipSdk.Client.dll The RFC 8829 §4.1.3 signalling state of a WebRTC IPeerConnection — the offer/answer half of the peer's lifecycle, distinct from the ICE/DTLS transport lifecycle exposed by PeerConnectionState. It mirrors the W3C RTCSignalingState, tracking where the peer sits in the SDP negotiation: whether an offer is pending locally, pending from the remote, or the exchange has settled. This SDK negotiates a single offer/answer exchange per peer (re-offer / renegotiation is a later package), so the state moves Stable → HaveLocalOffer → Stable (offerer) or Stable → HaveRemoteOffer → Stable (answerer) and then to Closed. The provisional-answer state (have-local-pranswer / have-remote-pranswer) is not used by this SDK — no a=pranswer path exists — and is therefore not modelled. public enum SignalingState Fields Closed = 3 The peer has been closed; no further negotiation is possible (RFC 8829 §4.1.3 closed). HaveLocalOffer = 1 A local offer has been produced (CreateOffer()) and applied, and the peer is waiting for the remote answer (RFC 8829 §4.1.3 have-local-offer — the offerer role). HaveRemoteOffer = 2 A remote offer has been applied and the peer is producing the local answer (RFC 8829 §4.1.3 have-remote-offer — the answerer role). Transient: the answerer moves through this state and back to Stable within a single SetRemoteDescriptionAsync(string, CancellationToken). Stable = 0 No offer/answer exchange is in progress: either none has started, or the last one completed. This is the initial state and the resting state between negotiations (RFC 8829 §4.1.3 stable).

SendRecv = 0 The track both sends and receives media (a=sendrecv), the default.
