_api/CalloraVoipSdk.WebRtc.WebRtcClient..summary: Class WebRtcClient Namespace CalloraVoipSdk.WebRtc Assembly CalloraVoipSdk.Client.dll The WebRTC peer facade (Level 1). Builds signalling-neutral IPeerConnections that run ICE, DTLS-SRTP, BUNDLE and RTP/RTCP internally; the app owns signalling and the codec (transport only). Zero-config new WebRtcClient() offers Opus over an ephemeral loopback endpoint with a fresh per-peer DTLS identity. See ADR-012 for the four-level design and the manager/DI tiers to come. public sealed class WebRtcClient : IWebRtcClient, IAsyncDisposable Inheritance object WebRtcClient Implements IWebRtcClient IAsyncDisposable Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Constructors WebRtcClient(WebRtcConfiguration?) Creates a client with the given configuration, or all defaults when omitted. public WebRtcClient(WebRtcConfiguration? config = null) Parameters config WebRtcConfiguration Properties Modules The registry of optional facade extensions contributed by separate packages (L3 plugin seam); register modules programmatically via Register(IWebRtcClientModule), or register IWebRtcClientModule services before AddCalloraWebRtc to have them auto-attached. public IWebRtcModuleRegistry Modules { get; } Property Value IWebRtcModuleRegistry Peers The registry of peer connections currently open on this client (L2 multi-peer manager). public IPeerConnectionManager Peers { get; } Property Value IPeerConnectionManager Methods CreatePeer() Creates a new peer connection with the client's configured codecs, DTLS identity and local endpoint. The caller drives signalling and disposes the returned peer. public IPeerConnection CreatePeer() Returns IPeerConnection DisposeAsync() Closes every peer connection still tracked by this client, then completes. Idempotent: a second call is a no-op. Each peer untracks itself as it disposes, so no dead peer is left registered. A failure in one peer's teardown does not prevent the others from being disposed; the first such error is rethrown. public ValueTask DisposeAsync() Returns ValueTask

_api/CalloraVoipSdk.WebRtc.WebRtcConfigu.title: Class WebRtcConfiguration | CalloraVoipSdk
_api/CalloraVoipSdk.WebRtc.WebRtcConfigu.summary: Class WebRtcConfiguration Namespace CalloraVoipSdk.WebRtc Assembly CalloraVoipSdk.Client.dll Immutable configuration for a WebRtcClient (the direct-construction surface; the DI/options path projects WebRtcOptions onto it). All fields are optional — a zero-config new WebRtcClient() binds an ephemeral loopback endpoint, offers Opus audio, and uses a fresh per-peer DTLS identity. public sealed class WebRtcConfiguration Inheritance object WebRtcConfiguration Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Remarks Immutable means immutable in fact, not by convention (#166 P2-7): every collection property takes a defensive copy of the list it is given, so a caller that keeps and later mutates its own list — including the mutable WebRtcOptions instance the DI path maps from — cannot reach into a live client's configuration. This is also the boundary where an unusable ICE-server entry is rejected, so the direct, options and builder paths agree instead of one failing fast and the others accepting silently. Properties AudioCodecs Audio codecs to offer, by name (opus, PCMU, PCMA, G722). Default: Opus. public IReadOnlyList<string> AudioCodecs { get; init; } Property Value IReadOnlyList<string> Exceptions ArgumentNullException The assigned list is null. DtlsCertificate DTLS-SRTP identity for the peer's certificate/fingerprint (must carry an exportable ECDSA P-256 private key); null generates a fresh ephemeral identity per peer — the WebRTC privacy default. public X509Certificate2? DtlsCertificate { get; init; } Property Value X509Certificate2 EnableVideo Whether to offer a video m-line. public bool EnableVideo { get; init; } Property Value bool IceServers STUN/TURN servers for gathering server-reflexive and relay ICE candidates (RFC 8445 §5.1.1). Empty (default) gathers only the host candidate. STUN entries are queried through the media socket when the app calls GatherCandidatesAsync(CancellationToken) — the discovered candidates surface on LocalIceCandidateDiscovered to trickle out (RFC 8838). public IReadOnlyList<IceServerConfiguration> IceServers { get; init; } Property Value IReadOnlyList<IceServerConfiguration> Remarks Only UDP TURN is supported for relay gathering; a TURN entry on TCP/TLS is rejected here rather than accepted into a client that would then silently gather no relay candidate (#166 P2-7, feature: #155). Exceptions ArgumentNullException The assigned list is null. ArgumentException A TURN entry uses a non-UDP transport. LocalEndPoint Local media endpoint the peer binds for RTP/RTCP/ICE/DTLS. Default is an ephemeral loopback port; production deployments set a reachable address. (Host-candidate advertisement and trickle ICE for remote reachability arrive in a later slice — see ADR-012.) public IPEndPoint LocalEndPoint { get; init; } Property Value IPEndPoint LoggerFactory Logger factory for diagnostics; null disables logging. public ILoggerFactory? LoggerFactory { get; init; } Property Value ILoggerFactory OpaqueVideoFrames Treats this peer's video frames as opaque: the app encrypts them end to end before handing them over (WebRTC Encoded Transform / SFrame, RFC 9605), so the SDK must never read the content. Default false keeps the clear-media payload format, which parses the frame to detect key frames. public bool OpaqueVideoFrames { get; init; } Property Value bool Remarks With the switch on, both halves of the video payload format work from the RTP framing alone: the frame is carried and reassembled verbatim, and IsKeyFrame is always false — "unknown", not "no", until the key-frame signal moves into a plaintext header extension (#223 follow-up). This is what makes "the provider cannot see the content" a property of the code rather than of its intentions (Anlage 31b BMV-Ä § 2 Abs. 3/4). Interop scope, stated rather than assumed: the opaque H.264 framing is self-consistent between two SDK endpoints and through a relay that forwards payloads untouched. It is not what a browser emits — a browser transform keeps the NAL headers in the clear — so do not enable it for a browser peer. See ADR-068. SimulcastLayers Send-side simulcast layers to offer (RFC 8853), by a=rid id in send order, e.g. ["hi", "mid", "lo"]. Empty (default) offers a single video stream. When set, the app sends each layer's encoded frames via SendVideoFrameAsync(string, ReadOnlyMemory<byte>, uint, CancellationToken) — the SDK packetises each on its own SSRC with the RID header extension (RFC 8852). Requires EnableVideo. This peer must be the offerer for the simulcast to be advertised. public IReadOnlyList<string> SimulcastLayers { get; init; } Property Value IReadOnlyList<string> Exceptions ArgumentNullException The assigned list is null. UseStableNumericMediaIds Makes a fixed 1+1 peer offer numeric MIDs from the first offer instead of the historic semantic audio/video MIDs. Runtime-added tracks (AddAudioTrack/AddVideoTrack) always use stable, append-only numeric MIDs regardless of this flag (RFC 8829 — existing m-lines never move or change MID), so it only affects the fixed 1+1 case. Default false keeps the byte-identical historic 1+1 SDP. public bool UseStableNumericMediaIds { get; init; } Property Value bool VideoCodecs Video codecs to offer when EnableVideo is set, by name (H264, VP8). Default: H264. public IReadOnlyList<string> VideoCodecs { get; init; } Property Value IReadOnlyList<string> Exceptions ArgumentNullException The assigned list is null.

_api/CalloraVoipSdk.WebRtc.WebRtcPeerCon.title: Class WebRtcPeerConnectionExtensions | CalloraVoipSdk
_api/CalloraVoipSdk.WebRtc.WebRtcPeerCon.summary: Class WebRtcPeerConnectionExtensions Namespace CalloraVoipSdk.WebRtc Assembly CalloraVoipSdk.Client.dll The signalling happy path (Level 1) for IPeerConnection: given an app-owned IWebRtcSignaling channel, the SDK drives the full offer/answer handshake and returns once the connection is established — the WebRTC counterpart to the SIP DialAndWaitUntilConnectedAsync. The neutral primitives (CreateOffer(), SetRemoteDescriptionAsync(string, CancellationToken), StartAsync(CancellationToken)) remain for callers that drive signalling themselves. public static class WebRtcPeerConnectionExtensions Inheritance object WebRtcPeerConnectionExtensions Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Methods ConnectAsync(IPeerConnection, IWebRtcSignaling, WebRtcRole, CancellationToken) Drives the SDP handshake over signalling for the given role and starts media, completing when the peer reaches Connected. public static Task ConnectAsync(this IPeerConnection peer, IWebRtcSignaling signalling, WebRtcRole role, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Parameters peer IPeerConnection signalling IWebRtcSignaling role WebRtcRole cancellationToken CancellationToken Returns Task Remarks Subscribe to TrackReceived before calling this so inbound tracks are not missed. Early-bind gives even an ephemeral (port 0) client a live offer m-line; a fixed, reachable media port is still recommended for NAT reachability without TURN. When signalling also implements IWebRtcTrickleSignaling, local candidates (host + server-reflexive) trickle out and remote candidates are applied during negotiation (ADR-012). Trickle contract: the remote-candidate pump is cancelled and awaited before this method returns. Your ReceiveCandidateAsync(CancellationToken) implementation SHOULD honour the supplied CancellationToken (return or throw OperationCanceledException when it fires), because that is what makes the teardown immediate. The SDK cannot force a non-cooperative channel to unblock, so the wait is bounded: after a short grace period the pump is abandoned and this method returns anyway — a channel that ignores its token costs a lingering background task, not a ConnectAsync that never returns on an already-connected peer (#166 P2-11). Exceptions ArgumentNullException peer or signalling is null. WebRtcConnectException The connection failed or was closed during negotiation. OperationCanceledException cancellationToken was cancelled.

Offerer = 0 The caller: creates the offer, sends it, then applies the remote answer (RFC 8829).

_api/CalloraVoipSdk.WebRtc.WebRtcStats.h.summary: Class WebRtcStats Namespace CalloraVoipSdk.WebRtc Assembly CalloraVoipSdk.Client.dll A point-in-time statistics snapshot for a peer connection (the SDK's getStats). Transport counters, derived bitrates, RTCP-derived quality, video, congestion-control and the ICE state/selected pair are all populated. A nullable metric reads null when it has not yet been measured (for example no media session is active, the peer has not yet reported, or no inbound video has been received) — a null value means "not yet measured", never a fabricated zero. public sealed class WebRtcStats Inheritance object WebRtcStats Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Properties AvailableOutgoingBitrateBps Estimated available outgoing bitrate in bits/second from transport-cc congestion control, or null until an estimate is available (no media session, or congestion control inactive for this leg). public long? AvailableOutgoingBitrateBps { get; init; } Property Value long? BytesReceived Total bytes of decrypted inbound RTP packets. public long BytesReceived { get; init; } Property Value long BytesSent Total bytes of protected RTP datagrams sent. public long BytesSent { get; init; } Property Value long ConnectionState The peer connection's current lifecycle state. public required PeerConnectionState ConnectionState { get; init; } Property Value PeerConnectionState DroppedDatagrams Inbound datagrams dropped (pre-key, auth failure, replay, or unroutable). public long DroppedDatagrams { get; init; } Property Value long FirCount Full Intra Request (FIR) messages sent. Always null: the bundle honours an inbound FIR as a keyframe request but never sends one itself, so this counter is never produced. public long? FirCount { get; init; } Property Value long? FramesDropped Frames dropped (e.g. by the reorder buffer), or null until a media session is active. public long? FramesDropped { get; init; } Property Value long? FramesPerSecond Inbound frames per second, or null until a media session is active. public double? FramesPerSecond { get; init; } Property Value double? IceState A W3C RTCIceConnectionState-style label (new/checking/connected/disconnected/failed/closed) derived from the peer's connectivity — the bundle uses single-candidate selection, not a separate ICE-checklist FSM. public string? IceState { get; init; } Property Value string IncomingBitrateBps Incoming bitrate in bits/second since the previous snapshot; null on the first snapshot. public double? IncomingBitrateBps { get; init; } Property Value double? JitterMs Our local receive-side interarrival jitter in milliseconds (RFC 3550 §A.8) — the WebRTC getStats inbound-rtp jitter — or null until an inbound clock rate is established (no media received yet). Converted from RTP timestamp units with the negotiated clock rate. This is the session aggregate — the worst (maximum) across inbound sources; the per-stream breakdown is in MediaStreams. public double? JitterMs { get; init; } Property Value double? KeyFrames Key frames received on inbound video, or null until a media session is active. public long? KeyFrames { get; init; } Property Value long? MediaStreams Per-media-stream quality (CF-004f): one entry per audio/video track (folded by MID) carrying the RTT and loss the peer reports on our outbound stream plus our local receive-side jitter for that track's remote inbound source, and one entry per remote inbound source whose payload type could not be attributed to a track. Empty until a session is built or a per-stream metric is available. The scalar RoundTripTimeMs/PacketLoss/JitterMs are the worst-of aggregate across these streams. public IReadOnlyList<WebRtcMediaStreamStats> MediaStreams { get; init; } Property Value IReadOnlyList<WebRtcMediaStreamStats> NackCount Generic NACK feedback messages sent, or null until a media session is active. public long? PacketLoss Fraction of our outbound packets the peer reports lost (0..1) via its RTCP reception report (RFC 3550 §6.4.1), or null until the peer has reported on our media. This is the session aggregate — the worst (maximum) loss across our sending streams; the per-stream breakdown is in MediaStreams. public double? PacketLoss { get; init; } Property Value double? _api/CalloraVoipSdk.WebRtc.html.title: Namespace CalloraVoipSdk.WebRtc | CalloraVoipSdk
_api/CalloraVoipSdk.WebRtc.html.summary: Namespace CalloraVoipSdk.WebRtc Classes AudioTrackOptions Deeper control for AddAudioTrack(AudioTrackOptions): the track's direction, its codec preferences, and the MediaStream it belongs to. Every field is optional — new AudioTrackOptions() yields a send-recv track using the client's configured AudioCodecs, matching the parameterless AddAudioTrack() happy path. Audio has no simulcast, so there is no per-layer/rid surface here. RemoteTrack A remote media track surfaced by TrackReceived (the W3C per-track model). Encoded frames arrive on FrameReceived. VideoTrackOptions Deeper control for AddVideoTrack(VideoTrackOptions): the track's direction, its codec preferences, send-side simulcast layers, and the MediaStream it belongs to. Every field is optional — new VideoTrackOptions() yields a send-recv track using the client's configured VideoCodecs, matching the parameterless AddVideoTrack() happy path. WebRtcClient The WebRTC peer facade (Level 1). Builds signalling-neutral IPeerConnections that run ICE, DTLS-SRTP, BUNDLE and RTP/RTCP internally; the app owns signalling and the codec (transport only). Zero-config new WebRtcClient() offers Opus over an ephemeral loopback endpoint with a fresh per-peer DTLS identity. See ADR-012 for the four-level design and the manager/DI tiers to come. WebRtcConfiguration Immutable configuration for a WebRtcClient (the direct-construction surface; the DI/options path projects WebRtcOptions onto it). All fields are optional — a zero-config new WebRtcClient() binds an ephemeral loopback endpoint, offers Opus audio, and uses a fresh per-peer DTLS identity. WebRtcConnectException Thrown by ConnectAsync(IPeerConnection, IWebRtcSignaling, WebRtcRole, CancellationToken) when the peer connection fails to establish — the connection reached Failed or was closed during negotiation (ICE or DTLS-SRTP did not complete). WebRtcMediaStreamStats A per-media-stream quality snapshot within a peer connection's WebRtcStats (the SDK's getStats per-stream breakdown). One entry per audio/video track (folded by MID), plus one per remote inbound source whose payload type could not be attributed to a track. The two directions carry different metrics — RoundTripTimeMs and PacketLoss describe our outbound stream (keyed per our sending SSRC, RFC 3550 §6.4.1), while JitterMs is our local receive-side jitter for the remote inbound source (RFC 3550 §A.8). A metric reads null until it is available for that stream — never a fabricated zero. WebRtcOptions Host-facing, mutable options for the WebRTC facade, consumed by AddCalloraWebRtc(...) — the dependency-injection counterpart to the immutable WebRtcConfiguration (mirrors how VoipOptions backs VoipConfiguration for the SIP facade). WebRtcPeerConnectionExtensions The signalling happy path (Level 1) for IPeerConnection: given an app-owned IWebRtcSignaling channel, the SDK drives the full offer/answer handshake and returns once the connection is established — the WebRTC counterpart to the SIP DialAndWaitUntilConnectedAsync. The neutral primitives (CreateOffer(), SetRemoteDescriptionAsync(string, CancellationToken), StartAsync(CancellationToken)) remain for callers that drive signalling themselves. WebRtcRecorder The built-in WebRTC recorder (L3 module). Attaches a media tap to a peer and streams every encoded frame (audio and video, both directions) into an IEncodedMediaSink. Usable standalone (new WebRtcRecorder().Start(peer, sink)) or registered as an IWebRtcClientModule and resolved via client.Modules.Get<IWebRtcRecorder>(). Transport-only: it captures the raw codec bitstream — turning it into a playable file is the sink's job. WebRtcStats A point-in-time statistics snapshot for a peer connection (the SDK's getStats). Transport counters, derived bitrates, RTCP-derived quality, video, congestion-control and the ICE state/selected pair are all populated. A nullable metric reads null when it has not yet been measured (for example no media session is active, the peer has not yet reported, or no inbound video has been received) — a null value means "not yet measured", never a fabricated zero. Structs BitrateRecommendation A ready-to-use send-bitrate recommendation for a peer connection, derived by the SDK from transport-wide congestion control (transport-cc). The SDK does the estimation and hands back a finished recommendation — the app sets its encoder (or, for an SFU, selects the simulcast layer to forward to this receiver) to this value; it never has to interpret raw delay/loss metrics. Carried by RecommendedBitrateChanged and mirrored point-in-time by RecommendedOutgoingBitrateBps. DtmfTone One fully received inbound DTMF tone (RFC 4733 telephone-event), surfaced on DtmfReceived once per tone after its end-of-event packet. EncodedFrame One encoded media frame received on a RemoteTrack. Transport-only: Payload is the raw depacketised codec bitstream — the app owns decoding. RecordedFrame One encoded media frame captured for recording, tagged with its track kind and direction. Transport-only: Payload is the raw depacketised codec bitstream (the recorder does not decode). Interfaces IAudioTrack A handle to an outbound audio track added with AddAudioTrack() (its own m=audio line on the shared BUNDLE transport, beyond the peer's primary audio anchor). Send encoded audio payloads on this track with SendFrameAsync(ReadOnlyMemory<byte>, uint, CancellationToken); each track carries its own SSRC, so payloads sent on distinct handles never collide (RFC 3550 §8.1). The SFU pattern of one audio stream per remote participant on a single peer connection. IEncodedMediaSink A destination for recorded encoded media. The recorder writes every captured RecordedFrame here (both directions, audio and video); the sink decides how to persist it — a per-track file, a container, an upload, an in-memory buffer, … Transport-only: payloads are the raw codec bitstream (no decoding). A container writer (Opus→Ogg, VP8→IVF, muxed MP4/…) is a concrete sink implementation. IMediaTap An L3 observer of the encoded media flowing through an IPeerConnection in both directions — the extension seam for recording, analytics, or feeding an AI pipeline without owning the peer. Attach with AttachMediaTap(IMediaTap) and dispose the handle to detach. IPeerConnection A signalling-neutral WebRTC peer connection: the app owns the signalling channel (WebSocket/HTTP/ Callora) and exchanges SDP through it, while this peer runs ICE, DTLS-SRTP, BUNDLE and the RTP/RTCP transport. Encoded media flows through SendAudioAsync(ReadOnlyMemory<byte>, CancellationToken)/SendVideoFrameAsync(ReadOnlyMemory<byte>, uint, CancellationToken) — the SDK is transport-only, so the app owns the codec. The central per-connection abstraction of the WebRTC facade, mirroring the SIP ICall. IPeerConnectionManager The L2 registry of peer connections opened through a IWebRtcClient — the WebRTC counterpart to the SIP ICallManager. Peers are tracked on creation and removed when disposed, so a multi-peer app (e.g. a conference) can enumerate its live connections without keeping its own list. IVideoTrack A handle to an outbound video track added before the first offer with AddVideoTrack() (its own m=video line on the shared BUNDLE transport). Send encoded frames on this track with SendFrameAsync(ReadOnlyMemory<byte>, uint, CancellationToken); each track carries its own SSRC, so frames sent on distinct handles never collide (RFC 3550 §8.1). IWebRtcClient The WebRTC peer facade — the happy-path entry point for building signalling-neutral peer connections. Mirrors the SIP IVoipClient; the advanced peer-registry manager tier is added in a later slice (ADR-012). Disposing the client asynchronously closes every peer it still tracks. Peer teardown is inherently asynchronous (IPeerConnection is IAsyncDisposable), so the client is async-disposable only; a DI host disposes it on the async path (an IHost, or an explicit await using / DisposeAsync on a manually built provider). IWebRtcClientModule Contract every WebRTC facade module implements to be discoverable through IWebRtcModuleRegistry — the L3 plugin seam, mirroring the SIP IVoipClientModule. Module packages define their own feature interfaces on top of this marker; the facade never references concrete module types. IWebRtcModuleRegistry Thread-safe registry resolving optional WebRTC facade modules by their feature contract. IWebRtcRecorder Records the encoded media flowing through a peer connection into an IEncodedMediaSink — an L3 module built on AttachMediaTap(IMediaTap). Transport-only: it captures the raw codec bitstream per track and direction; muxing to a playable container is the sink's job. IWebRtcRecording A running recording of a peer connection. Stop it with StopAsync(CancellationToken) (or by disposing) to detach from the peer and flush the sink. IWebRtcSignaling The app-owned signalling channel the SDK drives during ConnectAsync(IPeerConnection, IWebRtcSignaling, WebRtcRole, CancellationToken): a bidirectional transport (WebSocket, HTTP long-poll, Callora signalling, …) that carries SDP descriptions between the two peers. The SDK stays signalling-neutral — it only sends and receives SDP through this contract; the app decides how the bytes travel. IWebRtcTrickleSignaling Extends IWebRtcSignaling with out-of-band ICE candidate trickle (RFC 8838): alongside the offer/answer, the SDK sends each locally gathered candidate as it is discovered and applies remote candidates as they arrive, rather than relying only on the candidates the SDP carried. When an app supplies this on ConnectAsync(IPeerConnection, IWebRtcSignaling, WebRtcRole, CancellationToken), the SDK gathers server-reflexive candidates and runs the trickle exchange; a plain IWebRtcSignaling stays SDP-only. Candidate strings are RFC 8829 candidate:… lines — the wire form browsers exchange verbatim, so no conversion is needed at the app boundary. Enums MediaDirection The direction of media observed by an IMediaTap. PeerConnectionState Lifecycle state of a WebRTC IPeerConnection, modelled on the W3C RTCPeerConnectionState (RFC 8829): a signalling-neutral view of where the peer is between creation and teardown. ICE consent and the DTLS handshake drive the transitions. SignalingState The RFC 8829 §4.1.3 signalling state of a WebRTC IPeerConnection — the offer/answer half of the peer's lifecycle, distinct from the ICE/DTLS transport lifecycle exposed by PeerConnectionState. It mirrors the W3C RTCSignalingState, tracking where the peer sits in the SDP negotiation: whether an offer is pending locally, pending from the remote, or the exchange has settled. This SDK negotiates a single offer/answer exchange per peer (re-offer / renegotiation is a later package), so the state moves Stable → HaveLocalOffer → Stable (offerer) or Stable → HaveRemoteOffer → Stable (answerer) and then to Closed. The provisional-answer state (have-local-pranswer / have-remote-pranswer) is not used by this SDK — no a=pranswer path exists — and is therefore not modelled. TrackDirection The negotiated direction of a media track's m-line (RFC 3264 §5.1): whether this peer sends and/or receives media on it. Distinct from MediaDirection, which labels the in/out direction an IMediaTap observes; this is the SDP directionality a track is offered with. TrackKind The media kind of a remote WebRTC track surfaced by TrackReceived. WebRtcRole The negotiation role a peer takes in the SDK-driven handshake (ConnectAsync(IPeerConnection, IWebRtcSignaling, WebRtcRole, CancellationToken)).
